title: FTC weighs new duties for platforms carrying impersonation ads
description: Agency seeks evidence about ad tools and impersonation scams. No new platform rule has taken effect.
author: David Chen
body: The Federal Trade Commission is asking whether online platforms should face new obligations when their advertising tools help spread ads that impersonate businesses or government agencies. It has opened an advance notice of proposed rulemaking, not adopted a new rule.

The agency's September 24 notice focuses on ad-optimization services offered by social networks, search engines and digital marketplaces. It seeks evidence about how those tools select audiences and shape the delivery of ads, what platforms do to vet advertisers, and whether changes to the existing Impersonation Rule or a separate rule are warranted. Measures under consideration include advertiser screening, monitoring, removing confirmed scam ads and action against offending advertisers.

The FTC says consumers filed more than one million imposter-scam reports in 2025 and reported nearly $3.5 billion in losses. Those are reported losses, not an estimate of all fraud. The agency also says nearly 30% of consumers who reported losing money to scammers in 2025 said the first contact was on social media. Neither figure by itself proves a platform caused a particular loss.

The public comment deadline will be 60 days after the notice appears in the Federal Register. That publication date, rather than September 24, sets the clock. No new platform duty takes effect from this notice alone.

For people searching online for help with a bill or debt, the distinction between an official service and an ad that copies its name matters. Before providing account information or paying a supposed relief provider, navigate independently to the agency or provider's official site. Financialist's state-by-state debt help guide is a separate starting point for understanding state-specific debt rules; it is not a substitute for checking an offer's identity.

sources.label: FTC September 24 announcement on impersonation-ad rulemaking

title: September 28 tax deadline approaches for eligible San Carlos Apache Tribe disaster area taxpayers
description: Eligible taxpayers in the San Carlos Apache Tribe disaster area have a September 28 deadline for many postponed filings and payments.
author: James Park
body: Taxpayers covered by IRS disaster relief for severe storms and flooding in the San Carlos Apache Tribe area face a September 28 deadline for many postponed federal tax filings and payments. The relief is limited to eligible affected taxpayers; it is not a nationwide extension.

According to the IRS, qualifying individuals who live in the covered area and businesses whose principal place of business is there can use the postponement. Others whose records needed to meet a deadline are in the covered area can also qualify. The IRS lists additional categories, including eligible relief workers. The postponed window generally covers specified deadlines originally falling on or after October 10, 2025, and before September 28, 2026.

Estimated income tax payments that originally fell in that window are postponed through September 28. The IRS says affected taxpayers will not be penalized for failing to pay those installments if they pay by that date. Not every form or deposit is covered: the agency lists exceptions for certain information returns and employment and excise tax deposits. Anyone relying on the relief should check the complete IRS notice against their own filing obligation.

Eligible taxpayers in the federally declared disaster area may also choose whether to claim qualifying uncovered casualty losses for the disaster year or the prior year. The IRS says individual taxpayers have until October 15, 2026, to make that election. A casualty-loss claim involves separate eligibility and documentation rules; the postponed filing deadline does not automatically establish a deductible loss.

Financialist's Arizona debt-help guide covers a different topic, state debt rules, for readers managing obligations after the storm. It does not explain eligibility for federal disaster tax relief; use the IRS notice for that decision.

sources.label: IRS disaster tax-relief notice for San Carlos Apache Tribe area

title: Hawaii joins proposed Credit Acceptance auto-loan settlement with debt relief
description: Proposed multistate settlement offers potential cash restitution and debt relief for eligible Credit Acceptance borrowers.
author: James Park
body: Hawaii has joined a proposed multistate settlement with auto lender Credit Acceptance Corporation over allegations involving unaffordable loans and add-on products. The consent judgment still needs court approval in participating states, so the proposed relief should not be described as money already paid to every borrower.

In a September 23 announcement, Hawaii's Office of Consumer Protection said the nationwide settlement could provide up to $60 million in cash restitution and up to $634 million in debt forgiveness, with up to $15 million going to settling attorneys general. Those are nationwide maximums or prospective amounts, not a per-person payout. Hawaii expects eligible borrowers in the state to receive nearly $115,000 in direct payments in total and nearly $830,000 in debt relief in total, some of which the office says may already have been provided.

The state says investigators alleged that Credit Acceptance originated some loans it knew or should have known borrowers could not afford. They also alleged that dealers in its network added vehicle service contracts and guaranteed asset protection products without consumers understanding the purchase or believing the products were required to finance the car. These are allegations resolved by the proposed settlement, not findings in this article.

If approved, the judgment would require new disclosures, monitoring of add-on sales and a process to cancel certain products more easily. For qualifying risky loans made beginning December 2025 that fail quickly, the settlement describes a five-year program beginning November 2, 2026, under which qualifying borrowers would get 95% debt relief and would not face collection suits on those loans. Not every Credit Acceptance borrower qualifies.

The Hawaii office says Credit Acceptance must contact consumers entitled to certain types of relief. Borrowers should verify their eligibility through official channels and not assume that an unsolicited message requesting an upfront fee is legitimate. Financialist's Hawaii debt guide offers background on state debt rules, separate from the settlement's eligibility terms.

sources.label: Hawaii Office of Consumer Protection September 23 announcement

title: States reach $2.3 million Labcorp settlement over debt collector's data breach
description: Forty-four states reached an agreement with Labcorp over patient data held by a medical debt collector.
author: David Chen
body: A coalition of 44 state attorneys general has reached an approximately $2.3 million settlement with Labcorp over a 2019 data breach at a medical debt collector that handled Labcorp patient information. The agreement focuses on how the laboratory company oversees vendors holding sensitive patient data; the state announcement does not describe this $2.3 million as a consumer refund fund.

Delaware Attorney General Kathy Jennings announced the settlement September 24. The debt collector was Retrieval-Masters Creditors Bureau, doing business as American Medical Collection Agency, or AMCA. The breach potentially exposed information about more than 27.5 million people nationwide, including 10.2 million Labcorp patients, according to the Delaware announcement. "Potentially exposed" does not mean every person's data was misused.

Under the agreement described by Delaware, Labcorp will strengthen its vendor risk program, maintain an incident-response process for vendor security events, limit sharing of data where appropriate, and impose additional security standards and assessment requirements on debt-collection vendors. A third-party assessor will review its information-security program with a focus on vendor risk management. Labcorp's payment to the states is $2,287,455, including $30,135 to Delaware.

The state distinguishes this multistate agreement from a separate $35 million class-action settlement related to the breach. Consumers should not confuse the two or infer a personal payment from the states' agreement. The Delaware announcement does not set out a claims process for individuals under this state settlement.

Medical bills can reach a collector even when the original provider's name is more familiar to the patient. Anyone contacted about an old medical balance can ask for written details and check the debt independently before providing financial information. Financialist's state debt guides cover general collection rules by location; they do not determine whether someone was affected by this breach.

sources.label: Delaware Department of Justice September 24 announcement

title: Nano Banc deposits transfer to Sunwest after California closure
description: What customers can use this weekend and when the only branch reopens.
author: James Park
body: Nano Banc customers can continue using checks, ATMs and debit cards this weekend after California regulators closed the Irvine bank on Friday. The FDIC says Sunwest Bank of Sandy, Utah has agreed to assume substantially all Nano Banc deposits and buy some of its assets. Customers automatically become Sunwest depositors; the deposits Sunwest assumes remain FDIC-insured.

The FDIC says Nano Banc's only branch is scheduled to reopen Monday, September 28, under Sunwest during normal business hours. Checks written on Nano Banc accounts will continue to be processed, and loan customers should keep making their payments as usual. The agency says customers have immediate access to their deposits; they do not have to open a new account to make their assumed deposits available.

Nano Banc reported $686 million in deposits and $736 million in total assets as of June 30, according to the FDIC. Sunwest is buying approximately $476 million of assets; the FDIC will retain the rest for later disposition. The agency's preliminary estimate of the cost to the Deposit Insurance Fund is about $114 million. That is an estimated fund cost, not an amount charged to Nano Banc depositors; the estimate could change when assets are sold.

A bank closure often brings phishing attempts. Rather than follow a text claiming an urgent account migration, customers can use the FDIC's original notice for its official contact information and the bank's verified channels. FDIC deposit insurance coverage depends on account ownership and institution, not just an account balance. Financialist's bank-fees guide covers a different issue, overdraft rules, for people reviewing banking costs.

sources.label: FDIC September 25 Nano Banc closure notice

title: Maryland approves 2027 ACA rates: 14.6% average increase before subsidies
description: Regulator figures show why a market average and a household bill differ.
author: David Chen
body: Maryland approved 2027 health insurance premium rates on Friday. The state insurance regulator says unsubsidized individual Affordable Care Act plan premiums will rise 14.6% on average. That is a statewide market average, not a prediction of what every Maryland household will pay: a plan's price, the member's age and any subsidy can change the bill.

Maryland's published example makes the variation concrete. For a 40-year-old in the Baltimore metro area looking at the lowest-cost off-exchange silver plans, the listed monthly unsubsidized change ranges from $9 for an Optimum Choice HMO (from $342 to $350, as rounded in the regulator table) to $89 for a CareFirst PPO (from $585 to $674). These are sample plan figures, not statewide averages or quotes for a specific reader. An off-exchange example also does not show financial assistance available through Maryland Health Connection.

The Maryland Insurance Administration says roughly 70% of Maryland Health Connection users and 55% of the overall individual market receive a premium subsidy. The state has its own assistance program for eligible residents with household incomes below 400% of the federal poverty level. Those eligible for assistance may see a different net premium change from the 14.6% unsubsidized figure. The regulator says individual market enrollment stands at about 274,000, down from 294,000 last year.

Small-group premiums for employers with no more than 50 full-time employees are approved to rise 10.2% on average. That is below carriers' 13.1% requested increase. The regulator reports rising hospital and prescription costs as main drivers and puts the separate individual dental-market average increase at 3.0%.

Consumers should read their renewal notice and compare actual 2027 plans and assistance eligibility when enrollment opens. A health premium is not the same as a medical bill: Financialist's medical-debt guide explains ways to check and contest charges after care, not how ACA subsidies are calculated.

sources.label: Maryland Insurance Administration September 25 rate approval

title: IRS adds account notices and tax records to free mobile app
description: Official app adds selected account features; watch for tax-account lookalikes.
author: James Park
body: The IRS launched a renamed mobile app Friday, extending the older IRS2Go service with access to some Individual Online Account features. The agency says taxpayers can now use the free IRS app to view available balances, selected notices and tax transcripts, check refund or amended-return status and review payment activity. An account-specific feature may require secure sign-in; an app download by itself does not display private records.

Existing IRS2Go users do not need to download a separate replacement. The agency says normal app updates will deliver the new version for users with automatic updates enabled. The app is available in the Apple App Store and Google Play, and IRS.gov provides verified links. The IRS says the app does not replace the full website or its Business Tax Account and Tax Pro Account services. This first release extends selected individual features only.

For taxpayers with an approaching filing or payment deadline, the balance and payment-history features could be useful, but the app does not change the legal due date or automatically pay a balance. The IRS also says users may access an Identity Protection PIN through the app. Readers should not take a text message or search ad offering tax-account access as proof that an app is official: the IRS warns it will not request sensitive financial information through an unsolicited text, email or pop-up.

The September 28 disaster tax deadline for eligible San Carlos Apache Tribe-area taxpayers remains a separate IRS relief rule. Financialist's existing deadline report explains who is covered; the new app neither extends that window nor determines eligibility.

title: Michigan attorney general challenges UPPCO electric rate hike
description: A proposed 15.6% residential increase is not approved; state advocates a smaller increase.
author: James Park
body: Michigan's attorney general is asking regulators to cut a proposed Upper Peninsula Power Company electric rate hike. UPPCO seeks an additional $17.3 million in annual revenue, which the attorney general says would mean a 15.6% average increase for residential customers. Neither the company request nor the attorney general's counterproposal is an approved new customer rate.

In testimony filed jointly with the Citizens Utility Board of Michigan, Attorney General Dana Nessel argued Friday that any increase should be no more than $9.9 million, a cut of roughly 42% from the request. The attorney general also opposed UPPCO's requested return on equity increase from 9.86% to 10.55%, proposing instead 9.47%. These percentages concern the utility's allowed return, not the rate printed on a household bill.

Another household-level dispute is the residential fixed monthly charge. Nessel said the proposed $15 charge should be reduced to $10.87. A fixed charge applies even when a household uses less electricity, so its size can matter to customers who conserve power. The attorney general also objected to a proposed storm-restoration expense tracker that, she says, could lead to adjustments between the normal public rate cases. The Michigan Public Service Commission will decide the case.

UPPCO serves approximately 53,000 Upper Peninsula customers, according to the attorney general's office. A 15.6% average residential increase is not a quote for a particular home: usage, rate design and whatever the commission ultimately approves will determine that amount. Financialist's money-rights hub addresses other household expenses, including bank fees and medical bills; it does not calculate UPPCO electric charges. Customers should use their utility's rate documents and the commission's final order for bill-specific figures.

sources.label: Michigan Attorney General September 25 UPPCO testimony

title: Michigan sues generator sellers over customer deposits
description: State alleges customers paid deposits but did not receive generators or refunds.
author: David Chen
body: Michigan's attorney general filed a consumer-protection lawsuit seeking refunds for customers who allegedly paid deposits for home generators they never received. The case names Triple Circle, Double Circle, Goodrich Enterprise and Brad Scott, who, according to the state, were associated with two former Generator Supercenter franchise locations. The allegations have not been decided by a court, and a lawsuit is not a restitution payment.

The state says the franchises continued accepting thousands of dollars in deposits even as they were nearing closure. Its complaint alleges some customers never received generators or refunds, including customers who cancelled orders. The filing also alleges that business revenue, including consumer deposits, was used for personal purchases. Michigan filed the case in Kent County Circuit Court on September 8 and announced Friday that the defendants had been served this week.

According to the attorney general's account, the two franchise businesses were formed under agreements in late 2020 and the franchisor terminated those agreements in April 2024. The state seeks restitution and monetary damages for affected customers, an injunction and civil fines. It has not announced a claims deadline or an approved distribution amount.

Michigan residents who believe they are affected can contact the attorney general's Consumer Protection Team through the state website rather than pay a third party promising access to a refund. Documents such as the contract, deposit receipt, cancellation request and correspondence may help establish an individual claim. Financialist's Michigan debt guide is about collection rules, not this lawsuit, but can help readers facing separate bills while a disputed deposit remains unpaid.

sources.label: Michigan Attorney General September 25 lawsuit announcement

title: New York warns of storm price gouging: what to document
description: State alert explains the emergency-pricing standard and what a useful complaint records.
author: David Chen
body: New York's attorney general issued a consumer alert Saturday as a severe coastal storm was expected to bring heavy rain, wind and possible flooding to New York City, the Hudson Valley and Long Island. The warning concerns the price of essential goods and services during an emergency, not every price increase after a storm.

The attorney general's office says New York law bars businesses from taking unfair advantage by charging an unconscionably excessive price for goods or services vital to health, safety or welfare during an emergency. The state says the law covers New York vendors, including those selling online. Whether a particular charge breaks the law depends on its circumstances; the alert does not set a flat percentage threshold or make every expensive hotel room, generator or repair job a violation.

For a report, the office asks consumers to note the specific price increase, date and location. Save a receipt and take a photo of an advertised price where possible. A before-and-after price comparison can help an investigator understand the complaint, though the office decides whether to investigate and whether the legal standard is met. New Yorkers can submit a complaint through the attorney general's official website or call the number in its alert.

The office says violations may carry penalties of up to $25,000 per violation. That is a potential civil penalty on a business, not a consumer refund amount or a guarantee that a complaint will produce payment. Anyone hiring a storm-repair contractor should also get the full price and work scope in writing before paying a deposit. Financialist's New York debt guide explains separate rules for collecting a bill; it is not a guide to storm price-gouging complaints.

sources.label: New York Attorney General September 26 consumer alert
